topPRs.title: feat(agent): materialize exact restore candidate components (#20726)
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
## Scope

Adds exact quarantine-only character and file-set materializers for #20726.

## Guarantees

- Original validated character JSON bytes are preserved without defaults.
- Media, state-files, and vault materialize only below candidate quarantine.
- FD-bound no-follow nested writes use create-only publication and exact replay.
- Path UTF-8 order, size, digest, mode, millisecond mtime, device, and inode are proved.
- Symlink, hardlink, parent swap, Unicode duplicate, traversal, directory bomb, Proxy, and custom iterator inputs fail closed.
- No PGlite, live-layout commit, boot, activation, routing, or fallback-empty behavior.

## Proof

- Bun macOS: 33/33, 154 assertions.
- Node/Vitest on APFS: 33/33.
- Bun Linux root: 33/33, 154 assertions.
- Bun Linux UID 10001: 9/9, 48 assertions.
- Agent TypeScript, targeted Biome, and git diff --check: green.

Draft only. Do not mark Ready or merge without explicit authorization.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud): authorize exact restore candidate seals (#20726)
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
## Scope

Adds one-shot exact seal authorization and terminal candidate sealing for #20726, including a forward-only post-lock clock guard.

## Guarantees

- Raw CSPRNG proof remains only in bounded zeroizable memory; database stores digests only.
- Authorization expiry is checked with PRIMARY wall clock after authority locks.
- Append-only seal consumes exactly one authorization and produces exactly one terminal command.
- Lost COMMIT responses replay exact immutable bytes from PRIMARY after authority loss.
- Seal/seal and seal/abort races serialize fail closed.
- No materializer, boot, activation, routing, or cleanup execution.

## Proof

- PGlite: 1/1, 28 assertions.
- PostgreSQL 16 real: 1/1, 20 assertions, including expiry crossed under lock.
- Migrations 0370-0372: 9/9, 110 assertions.
- Migration journal: 6/6, 42 assertions.
- Shared contract: 11/11.
- TypeScript, targeted Biome, SQL whitespace, and git diff --check: green.

Draft only. Do not mark Ready or merge without explicit authorization.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud): add scoped Outreachr identity, Google, and billing integration
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Closes #30598. Adds the Eliza Cloud boundary required by Outreachr's hosted CRM.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] Targets `develop`; rebased onto `7bb7938d1e397` without conflicts.
- [x] Post-sync `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passed; `bun run verify` passed.
- [x] Reproducible behavior and validation limits are recorded below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto the latest fetched `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] Final post-sync verification passed at `8384d56f5c41d45f91eae3c1f08d79c96e981be7`.

# Risks

Medium: introduces a credential-bearing API boundary and a separate product's Stripe operations. Routes require a registered app and hashed client secret. User delegation is short-lived, revocable, and checked against primary account authority; Google ownership remains enforced by the managed connector service. Billing validates app/workspace/customer/price metadata and verifies Stripe webhook signatures. All new routes remain unavailable until explicit Outreachr bindings are configured.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Outreachr can exchange its existing app-login code for scoped identity and managed Google access without copying Google credentials into the CRM. The primary database retains an authorization-code digest so replay stays blocked even after grant revocation or a stale cache read. Google transport permits only the Gmail/calendar operations used by the CRM.

The billing boundary reuses Cloud's Stripe service for separate Outreachr workspace customers and monthly seat prices. Stable idempotency keys protect customer and checkout creation; current subscriptions are read from Stripe and webhooks are signature-verified. Existing Cloud products and subscriptions are not changed.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature; additive backend routes and an append-only delegation migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

Deployment bindings and migration order are documented in the companion Outreachr cloud README and implementation plan. Apply `0376_outreachr_delegations.sql` before enabling the routes; configure the exact app ID/origin/client-secret digest plus Sol/Astra price IDs and a dedicated webhook secret. Use the standard staging certification and production approval workflow.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`outreachr-delegation.test.ts`, `outreachr-billing.test.ts`, and `outreachr-delegations-migration.pglite.test.ts` under `packages/cloud/shared/src`.

## Detailed testing steps

- Run the three focused tests with Bun. Eleven tests passed at the final rebased head: app/client binding, verified active identity, expired/revoked grants, replay rejection, constrained Google transport, migration replay, Stripe customer/price ownership, exact seat pricing, and real Stripe SDK webhook signatures/tampering.
- `bun run verify` passed at the final rebased head: all 376 typecheck/lint tasks, Cloud API router/Worker bundle checks, and final repository audits. The final audit scanned 11,379 tests with zero focused tests and zero orphaned skips. Hosted run 33949880548 passed every check, including All Tests Passed.
- Cloud API typecheck includes router-contract checks and the production Worker dry run. The dry run bundled the new routes successfully.
- Companion Outreachr tests passed through real PostgreSQL and the real CRM command/connector/vault path using controlled provider responses, including approval, provider receipt persistence and duplicate-send rejection.
